title: sale_price doubles as high bid on unsold listings
description:
carsandbids_scraper_7day.py:257-259 writes the 'Bid to $X' figure into sale_price for unsold cars. 2,091 unsold rows carry a sale_price that is actually a high bid; where a row has both fields they disagree 15 times out of 17.

The field means two different things depending on the sold flag, so no consumer can trust it. Split before re-scraping or the ambiguity gets baked back in:
  sale_price -> completed sales only
  high_bid   -> top bid for every outcome, including sold

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
close_reason: Duplicate of CarsAndBidsData-dfu, which was filed first and covers the same defect. Current counts moved into dfu.

title: Scraper stopped emitting auction_status after 2026-03-02
description:
Every row with end_date >= 2026-03-02 has a blank auction_status; every row before it has one. 5,270 rows, five months of silent degradation.

Same window holds 1,889 of the 2,112 missing sale prices (2026Q1 333, Q2 1,062, Q3 494 — vs a ~15/quarter trickle before), and it is the same path that leaks the 'Save' button label into the model field.

One regression, three symptoms. Find what changed in the card/detail extraction around Mar 2026 and restore status capture before any backfill — re-scraping under the broken path just refills the same gap.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
notes:
ROOT CAUSE CORRECTED — the title's premise was wrong. Nothing 'stopped'; the scraper in this repo NEVER emitted auction_status. Its export_csv column list has no auction_status, high_bid or num_comments, and merge_master.py:84 reindexes fresh rows onto master's schema, filling absent columns with NaN by design.

The master CSV was hand-seeded with a historical dataset that HAD those columns. 2026-03-02 is simply where the incremental pipeline took over — the 'Backfill gap: Mar-Apr 2026' commit on 2026-05-01. Every row added since is blank.

num_comments is lost the same way (100% blank in the same window) and the dashboard reads it as its engagement signal. high_bid too.

FIX: read the outcome from the bid bar instead of inferring it from page prose. ul.bid-stats exposes labelled elements — li.ended holds the result phrase, span.bid-value holds the figure alone, li.num-bids and li.num-comments hold the counts. Verified live:
  Sold for $75,000       -> sold
  Sold After for $132,500 -> sold_after
  Auction Canceled        -> canceled
  Bid to $46,000          -> no_sale
Unrecognised phrases return None so the row stays visibly incomplete rather than being guessed into the wrong bucket.

Silent-drift guard filed separately as CarsAndBidsData-9x6.
close_reason: Scraper now emits auction_status, high_bid and num_comments, read from labelled bid-bar elements. Verified 4/4 against live auctions with known outcomes, plus an end-to-end scraper->merge_master run on a throwaway master copy confirming the columns survive the merge that was dropping them.

title: bool(nan) flags 487 status-less rows as sold in build_data.py
description:
build_data.py:200 does '1 if bool(r.get("sold", False)) else 0'. pandas reads the sold column as object dtype containing True/False/NaN, and bool(nan) is True — so every row with no sold value is packed as a sale.

Impact: 487 rows. All 487 also have no sale_price, so they compound CarsAndBidsData-35n — they land in the <$5k bucket AND inflate the sold count and STR.

Verified: build_data's coercion yields sold=27,334 vs 26,847 rows actually marked True.

Fix: 'r.get("sold") is True' instead of bool(...).

Note: line 201 applies the same bool() pattern to is_no_reserve. That column currently has zero NaNs (22,291 False / 14,232 True) so it is harmless today, but fix both for the same reason.
close_reason: Fixed: build_data.py now uses 'is True' instead of bool(). Rebuild output confirms sold 27,334 -> 26,847 (487 phantom sales removed).

title: Missing sale_price packed as $0, inflating the <$5k price bucket
description:
Sold listings whose price the scraper never captured are packed as 0 and counted as real sub-$5k sales.

Chain:
- build_data.py:196 safe_int(sale_price) turns NaN into 0
- tokens.js:108 first PRICE_BAND is {min: 0, max: 5000}
- data.js:494-503 computePriceDist counts any sold record with 0 <= p < 5000

Impact: 2,112 sold rows dataset-wide have no sale_price. They render as sub-$5k sales on every price distribution, and they sit in the sold denominator for GMV and avg price, understating both. Confirmed on the LC 500 model page: 9 bars in the <$5k bucket, 7 of which are $0 placeholders.

Confirming signal: computeScatterPoints (data.js:548) requires p > 0, so these rows are invisible in the scatter but present in the histogram — the 9-vs-2 discrepancy that surfaced this.

Fix: pack missing price as -1/null rather than 0; have computePriceDist, GMV and avgPrice skip those records; surface a 'price unknown: N' note so the omission is visible rather than silent.
close_reason: Fixed: missing price packs as PRICE_UNKNOWN (-1); hasPrice() guards every GMV/avg/median/distribution site. LC 500 <5k bucket 9 -> 2 (verified in rendered page); global 3,505 -> 906; avgPrice $24,636 -> $26,740.

title: Lazy-load details.json in the data layer
description:
Add loadDetails() to src/data.js: fetches public/data/details.json on first call, memoizes, and returns a lookup that resolves a record index to its detail fields (url, color, drivetrain, engine, location).

Must not be called from loadData() — the whole point is that the Overview payload is unchanged. Only the Model page triggers it, and it needs a loading state plus an error path that degrades to a tooltip without the extra fields rather than breaking the page.

Reconstruct the full url as 'https://carsandbids.com/auctions/' + path.

title: Emit details.json sidecar from build_data.py
description:
Add a second output, public/data/details.json, carrying the per-listing fields the tooltip needs and that are absent from the packed records: auction url path, exterior color, drivetrain, engine, location.

Dictionary-encode the low-cardinality fields (exterior_color 4,711 distinct; drivetrain 3; engine 735; location 8,275). Store the url as the path after 'https://carsandbids.com/auctions/' — all 33,021 rows share that prefix. Measured at ~2,079 KB raw / 693 KB gzip.

CRITICAL: build_data.py sorts records by month offset (line 141) before writing. The sidecar rows must be emitted in that same order so index i in details.rows corresponds to index i in records. Build both from the same sorted sequence rather than from the DataFrame order.

Verify: re-running produces a byte-identical auctions.json (git diff shows only the new file), and spot-checking 5 random indices matches the CSV row for that same year/make/model.

title: Model page: deep analysis of a single model's sales
description:
GOAL
A user can pick one model and see how that model's sales behaved over time — every sold auction plotted by date and price, shaded by mileage, with the full listing details and a link to the original auction one hover away.

SUCCESS CRITERIA
1. Selecting a model on the page plots every sold auction for it as date x price, point color grading with mileage, and the choice is reflected in the global filter chips.
2. Hovering a point shows year, make, model, mileage, bids, exterior color, and a working link to the carsandbids auction.
3. The four carried-over visuals (KPI row, STR vs GMV, price distribution, reserve split) all read the chosen model.
4. Re-running build_data.py leaves public/data/auctions.json byte-identical and emits details.json alongside it — proving the sidecar aligns to the record order without disturbing existing data.
5. Overview tab network payload is unchanged (600 KB gzip); details.json is fetched only on first visit to the Model page.

OUT OF SCOPE (tracked separately)
- unsold / high_bid / reserve-gap analysis — CarsAndBidsData-fty, -dfu
- zero-price sold listings — CarsAndBidsData-9q4
- scatter palette beyond 8 makes — CarsAndBidsData-4pr
- image thumbnails in the tooltip (image_url is only 60% filled)

CONSTRAINTS
- pandas is only importable via 'py -3', not the bash 'python'.
- build_data.py sorts records by month offset; the sidecar MUST be written in that same post-sort order or every tooltip mislabels. Highest-risk detail in this work.
- public/data/auctions.json is a committed 2 MB artifact — the rebuild must not churn it.
- Follow existing patterns: FilterContext for state, Card/CardHeader primitives, tokens.js for color, recharts for charts.

title: Scraper writes 'Bid to' into sale_price instead of high_bid
description:
carsandbids_scraper_7day.py:258 handles the unsold case as:

    elif 'Bid to' in parent_text:
        listing['sold'] = False
        listing['sale_price'] = parse_price(parent_text)

The high bid is stored in sale_price, and high_bid is not in the scraper's output columns (line 559). Result: 1,526 unsold listings in the master CSV carry a high bid in sale_price, and 1,538 records in the packed auctions.json have a nonzero price field while sold=0.

Inert today because every price aggregation in data.js gates on sold===1, so GMV and avg price are unaffected. But every future scrape adds more misrouted rows.

Fix: route to high_bid and add it to the output columns. Decide separately whether to backfill the existing misrouted rows.
notes:
SCRAPER HALF DONE in CarsAndBidsData-nql. The detail path now routes by outcome: sold -> sale_price and high_bid (a live sale clears at the winning bid); sold_after -> sale_price only (the live high bid is a different figure the page does not show); no_sale -> high_bid only; canceled -> neither. Both keys are assigned on every branch so the listing-card pass's 'Bid to' value cannot leak into sale_price.

Verified live: 9nY8BL4B now yields high_bid=46000 with sale_price empty.

REMAINING: the listing-card path (:257-259) still writes 'Bid to' into sale_price when detail scraping is skipped, and the client/packing side (CarsAndBidsData-fty) still needs high_bid in auctions.json. The 2,091 historical rows need the backfill.
close_reason: Card path now uses the same labelled-element read as the detail path, and apply_outcome() writes sale_price and high_bid on every branch so nothing leaks between passes. Verified on the live grid: 50 cards, 0 unsold rows carrying a sale_price, no_sale rows carry high_bid instead. Coverage check confirms the new selector detects everything the old text match did plus one more. Client-side packing remains in CarsAndBidsData-fty; the 2,091 historical rows in CarsAndBidsData-b1v.

title: Add brand and model filters to the sidebar
description:
Independent, multi-select brand and model filters in FilterSidebar, active on all five tabs via FilterContext.

Brand: pre-populated checkbox dropdown over all 170 makes with listing counts.
Model: typeahead resolving to exact-value chips (1,647 distinct model strings); suggestions scoped to selected brands when any are selected, but the two filters AND independently.

Plan: ~/.claude/plans/shimmering-conjuring-hopper.md

title: ~1,853 historical unsold rows keep a stale sale_price after the backfill
description:
Surfaced by a dry-run of backfill_outcomes.py --apply against a copy of the master CSV.

The backfill only re-scrapes its two target populations: the 2026-03-02+ window and the implausible-price rows. The misrouted 'Bid to' figures that CarsAndBidsData-dfu identified are mostly OUTSIDE both — historical no_sale rows with a plausible-looking price — so ~1,853 unsold rows still carry a sale_price once the backfill lands.

No scraping needed. For rows where the outcome is not a sale and sale_price is populated while high_bid is empty, the value IS the high bid and can be moved directly. Anything where both are populated needs a decision: dfu found they disagree 15 times out of 17, so they are not redundant copies.

Do this as a data migration after CarsAndBidsData-b1v applies, then assert the invariant: no row with sold=False may carry a sale_price.

title: merge_master silently fills master-only columns with NaN
description:
merge_master.py:84 does fresh.reindex(columns=master_df.columns), documented at :11-13 as 'master columns the scraper doesn't produce are filled with NaN'. That is what let auction_status and num_comments go 100% blank for five months without a single error — the pipeline reported success on every run.

Add a guard: when a column is populated in master but entirely NaN across the fresh rows, print a loud warning and, in CI, fail the step or surface it in the commit message. Schema drift between the scraper and the master should never again be silent.

Found while fixing CarsAndBidsData-nql.

title: Backfill re-scrape: 2026-03-02+ window plus the implausible-price URLs
description:
Roughly 5,500 pages: the 5,270 rows from the regression window plus the ~238 URLs with prices under $2,000 from any year.

Must run only after the capture fixes land (CarsAndBidsData-nql, -dxv, -ebc), otherwise it refills the same gaps. Deliberately not a full 36,523-row re-crawl — that risks rate-limiting and losing delisted auctions for little gain.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
notes:
Backfill must also recover num_comments, which is 100% blank across the same 5,270-row window and feeds the dashboard's engagement signal. Confirmed recoverable: li.num-comments is present on live pages.

Worked example of what the backfill will fix: 3zmVM2G4 is currently sold with no price; the live page shows 'Sold After for $132,500'.

title: Implement the outcome taxonomy end to end
description:
Replace the sold boolean with the mutually-exclusive outcome field agreed on CarsAndBidsData-ibh: sold, sold_after, reserve_not_met, no_bids, canceled, unknown.

Touches: scraper capture -> CSV column -> build_data.py pack (new field + schema bump) -> client STR/GMV/price-distribution semantics per the table on the epic. Headline STR counts live clears only, with an 'incl. sold-after' figure alongside; canceled leaves numerator and denominator both.

Depends on the capture bugs being fixed first — the taxonomy is only as good as the status the scraper actually sees.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh

title: Canceled auctions are badly under-detected (7 in five years)
description:
The 'canceled' status exists but has only 7 rows across 36,523 listings — implausibly low. The LC 500 at 9X6QO07z was a canceled auction yet is recorded as status 'sold' with a $729 price, so a canceled listing that still renders 'Sold'-ish text becomes a sale.

Under the settled taxonomy canceled auctions leave the STR denominator entirely, so detection accuracy now moves the headline STR — worth measuring the true population before publishing a revised rate.

Open question: whether C&B delists canceled auctions, which would make historical backfill impossible and limit this to forward capture.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
notes:
DETECTION FIXED in CarsAndBidsData-nql. 'Auction Canceled' in li.ended now maps to auction_status='canceled' with no price. Verified live on 9X6QO07z — the auction Matt identified, previously recorded as sold for $729.

REMAINING: the historical count is still 7, so the true canceled population is unknown until the backfill runs. Canceled pages ARE still reachable (9X6QO07z loaded fine), so historical backfill is possible — the earlier concern about delisting does not apply.

title: parse_price returns implausible two-digit prices on ~238 sold rows
description:
238 sold rows have a price under $2,000 on cars plainly worth far more: a 2022 Lucid Air Dream at $73, a Porsche Cayman S at $60, a 2021 Escalade at $9, a Focus RS at $45.

Distinct from the Mar-2026 regression: 237 of 238 carry status 'sold' (the OLD path) and they are spread evenly across 2021-2026 (15/45/59/43/67/9 by year). Roughly 0.9% of sold rows, steady for five years.

Suspected mechanism, unconfirmed: parse_price (:48-55) takes the FIRST $[\d,]+ in the parent element's whole inner text, and the detail loop (:400-410) lets the LAST h4 containing 'Sold' overwrite. Live pages return 403 unauthenticated, so confirming needs a Playwright run.

Fix: anchor the match to the 'Sold for' text, break on first match, and add a plausibility floor that flags rather than silently accepts. Then re-scrape the ~238 URLs.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
notes:
MECHANISM CONFIRMED and fixed at source in CarsAndBidsData-nql. The page puts the figure in its own element (span.bid-value inside li.ended), so the price is now read directly instead of regexing the first dollar amount out of a text blob. Verified on 9WZOOzbQ: yields 75000, the value that was being recorded as 80.

REMAINING: the ~238 historical rows still carry the bad values and need the targeted re-scrape (CarsAndBidsData-b1v). A plausibility floor that flags suspiciously low sale prices is still worth adding as a safety net.

title: Rework scraper auction-outcome capture: complete outcome taxonomy + price anchoring
description:
Root cause behind CarsAndBidsData-35n and -fke. Needs design discussion BEFORE re-scraping — the goal is a complete, correctly-bucketed picture of auction outcomes, not just a price patch.

Known defects in scripts/carsandbids_scraper_7day.py:
- :254-259 card path only sets sale_price when card text contains 'Sold for' or 'Bid to'. Any other layout leaves sold/price unset with no error.
- :409 detail path assigns only 'if price:', so sold=True with price=None is a silent reachable state.
- :48-55 parse_price grabs the FIRST $[\d,]+ in the parent element's whole inner text.
- :400-410 loops every h4 containing 'Sold' and lets the LAST match overwrite, so a stray dollar figure beats the real sale price.
- No concept of a canceled auction — a canceled listing rendering 'Sold' text is recorded as a sale.

Known-bad examples: 9X6QO07z recorded $729 (auction was canceled); 9WZOOzbQ recorded $80 (actually sold ~$75k).

Open design question to settle first: the full auction outcome taxonomy (sold live, sold after auction, reserve not met, canceled/withdrawn, scrape-failed/unknown) and how each maps to the sold flag, STR numerator/denominator, GMV, and price distribution.

Live pages return 403 to unauthenticated fetches, so verification requires a Playwright run.
design:
SETTLED DESIGN (decided 2026-08-13).

Outcome taxonomy — one mutually-exclusive field replacing the sold boolean:
  sold             -> STR numerator + denominator, GMV, price distribution
  sold_after       -> denominator + GMV/price dist; NOT in headline STR numerator.
                      Report headline STR (live clears only) AND an 'incl. sold-after' figure.
  reserve_not_met  -> denominator only; carries high_bid
  no_bids          -> denominator only (split from no_sale: no demand vs demand below reserve)
  canceled         -> EXCLUDED from numerator AND denominator; reported as its own count.
                      A canceled auction never got a fair test, so counting it as a failure
                      understates STR.
  unknown          -> excluded from everything, counted and surfaced in the UI

Money fields, disambiguated:
  sale_price -> only ever a completed sale price
  high_bid   -> top bid for EVERY outcome, including sold (currently blank on sold rows)

Backfill scope: the 2026-03-02+ regression window (5,270 rows) plus ~238 URLs with
implausible prices from any year. Not a full re-crawl.

title: Non-vehicle lots are silently attributed to the make 'AC'
description:
build_data.py packs make as make_ix.get(safe_str(r.get('make')), 0). When make is blank the .get() default of 0 assigns index 0, which is a real make — 'AC'.

7 rows in the master CSV have blank make and model. They are not cars: Formula 1 ticket packages, Petit Le Mans VIP, a ride-along experience, One Lap of America entry, and two charity/experience lots. All 7 are packed as make 'AC'.

Result: 8 records carry make index 0 while only 1 is genuinely an AC, so that make is inflated 8x in Volume by Make and any per-make aggregate.

Options: drop non-vehicle lots at build time (they have no year/make/model and cannot be analysed), or add an explicit 'Unknown' make rather than defaulting to index 0. Prefer dropping — they are not auctions of vehicles and pollute every make-level metric.

Found while verifying details.json alignment; the sidecar itself is correctly aligned for these rows.

title: Date vs price scatter with mileage gradient and rich tooltip
description:
The page's core visual. x = date of sale (FIELD.dy, day offset from 2021-08-01), y = sale price, point fill a continuous gradient encoding mileage, with a legend for the scale.

Sold listings only. Must read well from n=1 to n=1,177 (3 Series is the largest model; 524 models have a single listing).

Needs a year-aware x-axis formatter — the existing dayLabel() in tokens.js emits 'Jan 15' with no year, which is ambiguous across a 5-year span.

Tooltip carries year, make, model, mileage, bids, views, exterior color, reserve status, and a clickable link to the auction.

Load the dataviz and dataviz-conventions skills before writing chart code — the gradient must stay legible in both light and dark themes.

title: Model page scaffold, tab wiring, and single-select picker
description:
New src/tabs/ModelTab.jsx plus wiring: add 'Model' to the tabs array in Header.jsx:33 and a branch in App.jsx alongside the other tabs.

Page owns a prominent single-select model typeahead, reusing FilterMultiSelect's typeahead mode (or a single-select variant of it) and writing the choice to filters.models as a one-element array, so the sidebar chip and every other tab stay consistent.

Empty state when no model is chosen; if arriving with exactly one model already selected, analyze it automatically; if several are selected, focus one and offer a switch.

title: Pack high_bid into auctions.json for reserve-gap analysis
description:
Enables analysing where bidding stalls on no-sale auctions vs what comparable cars actually sold for.

Coverage available without any re-scraping (8,789 unsold listings):
  high_bid column:              3,714
  misrouted into sale_price:    1,526
  both:                            17
  recoverable now:              5,257 (59.8%)
  needs a re-scrape:            3,532 (40.2%)

Coverage of the high_bid column alone is a stable ~44% across 2021-2025 (44.3/44.5/43.7/44.4/44.6), dropping to 26% for 2026 — so it is a consistent sample, not era-biased.

CAUTION: where both high_bid and sale_price are present (17 rows), they agree in only 2. Spot-check against the live site to determine which source is authoritative before merging them.

Any UI must show the denominator rather than presenting an average over the ~60% as 'the' figure.

Deferred deliberately — see also the incorrect comment in bd about estimatedLostGMV.

title: passesUniverse resolves makes with indexOf per record
description:
src/data.js:77 does DATA.makes.indexOf(name) inside the per-record predicate, for each selected make: up to 170 string compares x 33k records x N makes on every filter change.

The new brand dropdown makes selecting many makes at once easy, so this path is newly reachable. Fix: hoist the selected makes into a Set of indices outside the record loop.

Deliberately left out of the brand/model filter change to keep that diff minimal.

title: Measure lost GMV from real high bids instead of estimating it
description:
computeSTRHeadlineStats estimates lost GMV as failedCount x avgSalePrice, and its comment claims unsold high bids are not in the dataset. That is wrong: 3,731 unsold rows carry high_bid directly and another 2,091 have it stashed in sale_price — 5,805 of 9,189 unsold listings, 63%.

Once CarsAndBidsData-dxv separates the two fields, lost GMV can be summed from actual top bids for the rows that have them, with the estimate used only for the remaining 3,384. Also fix the stale comment.

Parent: CarsAndBidsData-ibh
close_reason: Duplicate of CarsAndBidsData-lrf (fix the estimate + comment) and CarsAndBidsData-fty (pack high_bid), both filed first. Current counts moved into lrf.

title: Carry over the four model-scoped visuals
description:
Scoped to the chosen model, reusing the existing aggregations in data.js rather than writing new ones:
  KPI row              — computeKPIs
  STR vs Total GMV     — computeByMonthSplit
  Price distribution   — computePriceDist
  Reserve vs No Reserve— computeReserveSplit

Match the existing card styling (Card / CardHeader from Primitives.jsx). Handle the thin-data case: a model with 3 sales should not render a misleading monthly trend line.

title: 1,023 sold listings have zero sale price and are dropped from GMV
description:
In packed auctions.json, 1,023 records have sold=1 and price=0. computeKPIs and every GMV aggregation add r[FIELD.p] for sold records, so these contribute 0 and understate GMV. They still count toward totalSold, so avgPrice (gmv/soldCount) is also dragged down.

In the source CSV, 877 sold rows have no sale_price (99.0% of 'sold'-status rows are filled, so the gap is mostly the 1,768 blank-status rows).

Decide whether to exclude them from the sold denominator, backfill, or leave and document.
close_reason: Superseded by CarsAndBidsData-35n, which covers the same defect with current numbers (2,112 sold rows missing price, not 877) plus the bool(nan) sold-inflation found alongside it. Fixed there.

title: computeSTRHeadlineStats comment wrongly claims high_bid is unavailable
description:
src/data.js:684 states 'high_bid for unsold listings is not in the dataset', and estimatedLostGMV therefore approximates lost value as failed-reserve count x avg sale price across all sold listings.

That is true of the packed auctions.json but false of the source CSV, which has high_bid populated for 3,731 no-sale listings (plus 1,526 more misrouted into sale_price).

Once high_bid is packed, estimatedLostGMV can use real high bids where present and fall back to the average only for the remainder. Fix the comment either way.
notes: Re-measured 2026-08-13: 3,731 unsold rows carry high_bid directly, plus 2,091 with it misrouted into sale_price. Recoverable without re-scraping: 5,805 of 9,189 unsold listings (63%). The remaining 3,384 still need the estimate.

title: Scatter reuses colors past 8 selected makes
description:
OverviewTab switches the mileage-vs-price scatter into per-make color mode at filters.makes.length >= 2, indexing MAKE_COLORS (8 entries) with % length. Selecting 9+ brands silently reuses colors, so two series look identical in the chart and legend.

Pre-existing, but the new brand dropdown makes 9+ selections easy to reach. Options: extend the palette, cap colored series and group the tail as Other, or warn in the legend.
